text: In the seventh year Jehoiada took courage and brought the commanders of hundreds into a covenant with him: Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri.

versions.text: In the seventh year Jehoiada took courage and made a covenant with the commanders of hundreds: Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew says Jehoiada "took" the commanders into covenant "with him" (עִמּוֹ בַבְּרִית), stressing his initiative in enlisting them. "Made a covenant with" loses the nuance of him drawing them in; the revised wording keeps both the action and the reciprocal "with him."

text: They traveled throughout Judah and gathered the Levites from all the towns of Judah, along with the heads of the families of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem.
Then the whole assembly made a covenant with the king in the house of God. Jehoiada said to them, "Here is the king's son! He shall reign, just as the LORD promised concerning the sons of David.
This is what you are to do: a third of you priests and Levites who come on duty on the Sabbath are to guard the doors,
a third are to be at the royal palace, and a third at the Foundation Gate, while all the people are to be in the courts of the house of the LORD.
No one is to enter the house of the LORD except the priests and the Levites who minister there; they may enter, for they are consecrated. But all the people are to keep the watch of the LORD.

versions.text: No one is to enter the house of the LORD except the priests and the Levites on duty; they may enter, for they are consecrated. All the rest of the people are to keep the watch of the LORD.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads simply "all the people" (וְכָל־הָעָם); "the rest of" is an addition. Also הַמְשָׁרְתִים לַלְוִיִּם refers to the Levites who minister (serve) in the temple rather than a rotation "on duty," which is already covered in verse 4.

text: The Levites are to surround the king, each man with his weapons in his hand, and anyone who enters the temple is to be put to death. Stay close to the king wherever he goes."

The Levites and all Judah did everything Jehoiada the priest had commanded. Each of them took his men—those coming on duty on the Sabbath and those going off duty—for Jehoiada the priest had not released any of the divisions.
Jehoiada the priest gave the commanders of hundreds the spears and the large and small shields that had belonged to King David and were kept in the house of God.
He stationed all the people, each man with his weapon in his hand, around the king—from the right side of the temple to the left, near the altar and the temple.
Then they brought out the king's son, put the crown on him, gave him the testimony, and proclaimed him king. Jehoiada and his sons anointed him, and they shouted, "Long live the king!"
When Athaliah heard the noise of the people running and praising the king, she came to them at the house of the LORD.

She looked, and there was the king, standing by his pillar at the entrance, with the officers and the trumpeters beside him. All the people of the land were rejoicing and blowing trumpets, and the singers were leading the praise with their instruments. Then Athaliah tore her clothes and cried out, "Treason! Treason!"

Jehoiada the priest brought out the commanders of hundreds who were in charge of the troops and said to them, "Take her out between the ranks, and put to the sword anyone who follows her." For the priest had said, "Do not put her to death in the house of the LORD."
So they seized her, and when she reached the entrance of the Horse Gate at the royal palace, they put her to death there.
Then Jehoiada made a covenant between himself and all the people and the king, that they would be the LORD's people.
All the people went to the temple of Baal and tore it down. They smashed its altars and its images, and they killed Mattan, the priest of Baal, in front of the altars.

Then Jehoiada placed the oversight of the house of the LORD in the hands of the priests, who were Levites, whom David had assigned to the house of the LORD, to offer the burnt offerings of the LORD as written in the Law of Moses, with rejoicing and song, as David had directed.
He also stationed gatekeepers at the gates of the house of the LORD, so that no one who was unclean in any way could enter.

Then he took the commanders of hundreds, the nobles, the rulers of the people, and all the people of the land, and brought the king down from the house of the LORD. They went through the Upper Gate into the palace and seated the king on the royal throne.
All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet, for they had put Athaliah to death with the sword.

versions.text: All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet, for Athaliah had been put to the sword.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb is active ("they put Athaliah to death with the sword"). The active form is also stronger and clearer for oral reading than the passive "had been put to the sword."
